deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls if Terraform may delete the webhook, abandon it from Terraform managmeent, or prevent its destruction. A policy should require PREVENT to reduce the risk of accidental or unauthorised removal that could disrupt the agent's webhook integration.

disabled.description: Indicates whether the webhook is disabled.
disabled.rationale: Controls if Dialogflow can invoke the webhook. The appropriate state depends on if the agent requires the integration, so forcing the webhook to be either enabled or disabled would be an operational decision rather than a generic security control.

display_name.description: The human-readable name of the webhook, unique within the agent.
display_name.rationale: Sets the human-readable name used to identify the webhook. It does not control authentication, access, encryption, network exposure, or data handling, so it is not a generic security policy target.

enable_spell_correction.description: Deprecated. Indicates if automatic spell correction is enabled in detect intent requests.
enable_spell_correction.rationale: Controls the automatic spell-correction behaviour used when processing detect-intent requests. This affects how user input is interpreted rather than authentication, access, encryption, exposure, or another generic security control.

enable_stackdriver_logging.description: Deprecated. Determines whether this agent should log conversation queries.
enable_stackdriver_logging.rationale: Controls whether Dialogflow activity, including webhook requests, responses, and errors, are recorded in Cloud Logging. A policy should require logging to remain enabled to preserve visibility for security monitoring, incident investigation, and auditing.

parent.description:
The agent to create a webhook for.
Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/agents/<Agent ID>.
parent.rationale: Identifies the Dialogflow CX agent that owns the webhook. It is a team-specific resource reference, and constraining it would require pinning a particular project, location, or agent rather than improving the webhook's security.

security_settings.description: Deprecated. Name of the SecuritySettings reference for the agent. Format: projects/<Project ID>/locations/<Location ID>/securitySettings/<Security Settings ID>.
security_settings.rationale: References an existing Dialogflow CX SecuritySettings resource that separately controls data redaction and retention. This field only selects a team-specific resource path, so the security controls should be assessed on the referenced resource rather than by constraining its identifier here.

timeout.rationale: Sets how long Dialogflow waits for the webhook response before treating the execution as failed. It is an availability and performance tuning value whose appropriate setting depends on the workload, with no generic secure duration to enforce.

generic_web_service.description: Represents configuration for a generic web service.

generic_web_service.allowed_ca_certs.description:
Specifies a list of allowed custom CA certificates (in DER format) for
HTTPS verification. This overrides the default SSL trust store. If this
is empty or unspecified, Dialogflow will use Google's default trust store
to verify certificates.
N.B. Make sure the HTTPS server certificates are signed with "subject alt
name". For instance a certificate can be self-signed using the following
command,
openssl x509 -req -days 200 -in example.com.csr \
-signkey example.com.key \
-out example.com.crt \
-extfile <(printf "\nsubjectAltName='DNS:www.example.com'")
generic_web_service.allowed_ca_certs.rationale: Defines custom certificate authorities that replace Google's default trust store when validating the webhook's HTTPS certificate. A policy should normally require this list to remain empty or restrict custom CA use to approved exceptions so that untrusted or self-signed certificate authorities do not unnecessarily broaden the webhook's TLS trust boundary.

generic_web_service.http_method.description:
HTTP method for the flexible webhook calls. Standard webhook always uses
POST. Possible values: ["POST", "GET", "HEAD", "PUT", "DELETE", "PATCH", "OPTIONS"]
generic_web_service.http_method.rationale: Selects the HTTP verb used for flexible webhook calls. The correct verb is determined by the target API contract, and none of the supported methods is inherently a universally insecure choice, so it is not a generic security policy target.

generic_web_service.parameter_mapping.description:
Maps the values extracted from specific fields of the flexible webhook
response into session parameters.
- Key: session parameter name
- Value: field path in the webhook response
generic_web_service.parameter_mapping.rationale: Maps fields from a flexible webhook response into Dialogflow session parameters. These application-specific mappings implement the team's conversation logic, and no generic secure mapping can be enforced without knowing that logic.

generic_web_service.request_body.description: Defines a custom JSON object as request body to send to flexible webhook.
generic_web_service.request_body.rationale: Defines the application-specific JSON body sent by a flexible webhook. It is a free-form request document whose required fields and session parameters depend on the target API, so a generic platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain it.

generic_web_service.request_headers.description: The HTTP request headers to send together with webhook requests.
generic_web_service.request_headers.rationale: Defines inline HTTP headers and can contain static authorisation credentials. A policy should reject secret-bearing headers, particularly inline Authorization values, and require sensitive header values to use secret_versions_for_request_headers while still permitting non-sensitive functional headers.

generic_web_service.secret_version_for_u.description:
The SecretManager secret version resource storing the username:password
pair for HTTP Basic authentication.
Format: 'projects/{project}/secrets/{secret}/versions/{version}'
generic_web_service.secret_version_for_u.rationale: Enables HTTP Basic authentication using a static username and password stored in Secret Manager. Although Secret Manager protects the credential, Basic authentication remains a weak static-auth mechanism, so a policy should require this field to be unset in favour of managed token, service-account, or OAuth authentication where supported.

generic_web_service.service_agent_auth.description:
Indicate the auth token type generated from the [Diglogflow service
agent](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-agents#dialogflow-service-agent).
The generated token is sent in the Authorization header. Possible values: ["NONE", "ID_TOKEN", "ACCESS_TOKEN"]
generic_web_service.service_agent_auth.rationale: Selects whether webhook requests use no service-agent token, an ID token, or an access token. A policy should disallow NONE where this is the selected authentication mechanism and require an appropriate token type so the receiving service can authenticate the Dialogflow caller.

generic_web_service.uri.description: The webhook URI for receiving POST requests. It must use https protocol.
generic_web_service.uri.rationale: Specifies the endpoint that receives webhook requests and potentially sensitive conversation data. A policy should require the https:// scheme so requests are encrypted in transit, while leaving the team-specific host and path unconstrained.

generic_web_service.webhook_type.description: Type of the webhook. Possible values: ["STANDARD", "FLEXIBLE"]
generic_web_service.webhook_type.rationale: Selects standard or flexible webhook request and response behaviour. Both are supported functional designs, and neither webhook type is inherently a weaker security configuration.

generic_web_service.oauth_config.description:
Represents configuration of OAuth client credential flow for 3rd party
API authentication.

generic_web_service.oauth_config.client_.description: The client ID provided by the 3rd party platform.
generic_web_service.oauth_config.client_.rationale: Identifies the third-party OAuth client. It is a non-secret, team-specific identifier, and a generic policy cannot constrain it without pinning a particular external client.

generic_web_service.oauth_config.client_.description:
The client secret provided by the 3rd party platform.  If the
'secret_version_for_client_secret' field is set, this field will be
ignored.
generic_web_service.oauth_config.client_.rationale: Supplies the OAuth client secret directly in configuration. Google recommends storing this credential in Secret Manager, so a policy should require this inline field to be unset and use secret_version_for_client_secret instead.

generic_web_service.oauth_config.scopes.rationale: Defines the permissions requested for the third-party OAuth access token. A policy should require explicit, appropriately narrow scopes and reject empty, wildcard-like, or known overly broad scopes to reduce the privileges available through a compromised token.

generic_web_service.oauth_config.secret_.description:
The name of the SecretManager secret version resource storing the
client secret. If this field is set, the 'client_secret' field will be
ignored.
Format: 'projects/{project}/secrets/{secret}/versions/{version}'
generic_web_service.oauth_config.secret_.rationale: References the Secret Manager version containing the OAuth client secret. This is the recommended storage mechanism, but its value is a team-specific resource reference whose protection should be enforced through Secret Manager IAM rather than by constraining the referenced name.

generic_web_service.oauth_config.token_e.description:
The token endpoint provided by the 3rd party platform to exchange an
access token.
generic_web_service.oauth_config.token_e.rationale: Specifies the endpoint to which OAuth client credentials are sent to obtain an access token. A policy should require an https:// endpoint to protect credentials and returned tokens in transit, without constraining the team-specific identity-provider host.

generic_web_service.secret_versions_for_.description:
The HTTP request headers to send together with webhook requests. Header
values are stored in SecretManager secret versions.

When the same header name is specified in both 'request_headers' and
'secret_versions_for_request_headers', the value in
'secret_versions_for_request_headers' will be used.
The identifier for this object. Format specified above.
generic_web_service.secret_versions_for_.rationale: Names the HTTP header whose value is retrieved from Secret Manager. The correct header name depends on the target service's authentication contract, and the name itself is neither a credential nor a generic security control.

generic_web_service.secret_versions_for_.description:
The SecretManager secret version resource storing the header value.
Format: 'projects/{project}/secrets/{secret}/versions/{version}'
generic_web_service.secret_versions_for_.rationale: References the Secret Manager version containing the HTTP header value. Using Secret Manager is the secure storage mechanism, but the version path is a team-specific resource reference whose protection is governed by Secret Manager IAM.

generic_web_service.service_account_auth.description: Configuration for authentication using a service account.

The email address of the service account used to authenticate the webhook call.
Dialogflow uses this service account to exchange an access token and the access
token is then sent in the **Authorization** header of the webhook request.

The service account must have the **roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator** role
granted to the
[Dialogflow service agent](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-agents?_gl=1*1jsujvh*_ga*NjYxMzU3OTg2LjE3Njc3MzQ4NjM.*_ga_WH2QY8WWF5*czE3Njc3MzQ2MjgkbzIkZzEkdDE3Njc3MzQ3NzQkajYwJGwwJGgw#dialogflow-service-agent).
generic_web_service.service_account_auth.rationale: Selects the service account whose access token authenticates the webhook request and therefore determines the permissions available to the call. A policy should reject default service accounts and require a dedicated identity, without pinning a specific account, to support least privilege.

service_directory.description: Configuration for a Service Directory service.

service_directory.service.description: The name of Service Directory service.
service_directory.service.rationale: Identifies the Service Directory service used to resolve the webhook's private endpoint. It is a team-specific resource reference, and constraining it would require pinning a particular project, location, namespace, or service rather than enforcing a generic security property.

service_directory.generic_web_service.description: Represents configuration for a generic web service.

service_directory.generic_web_service.al.description:
Specifies a list of allowed custom CA certificates (in DER format) for
HTTPS verification. This overrides the default SSL trust store. If this
is empty or unspecified, Dialogflow will use Google's default trust store

N.B. Make sure the HTTPS server certificates are signed with "subject alt
name". For instance a certificate can be self-signed using the following

openssl x509 -req -days 200 -in example.com.csr \
-signkey example.com.key \

service_directory.generic_web_service.al.rationale: Defines custom certificate authorities that replace Google's default trust store when validating the Service Directory webhook's HTTPS certificate. A policy should normally require this list to remain empty or restrict custom CA use to approved exceptions so that untrusted or self-signed certificate authorities do not unnecessarily broaden the TLS trust boundary.

service_directory.generic_web_service.we.rationale: Selects standard or flexible webhook request and response behaviour. Both are supported functional designs, and neither webhook type is inherently a weaker security configuration.

When the same header name is specified in both 'request_headers' and

The identifier for this object. Format specified above.
service_directory.generic_web_service.se.rationale: Names the HTTP header whose value is retrieved from Secret Manager for the Service Directory webhook. The correct header name depends on the target service's authentication contract, and the name itself is neither a credential nor a generic security control.

service_directory.generic_web_service.se.description:
The SecretManager secret version resource storing the header value.
Format: 'projects/{project}/secrets/{secret}/versions/{version}'
